pages.text: The falling river left several pools on the bank. Small fish were trapped in each. Mina had seen them during the day.
Mina looked up at the sun outside. "I'll see the pools before sunset!" First, the housework had to be finished.
Mom divided the jobs: Raju swept the yard, Mina washed dishes, and Sonu set out spoons.
Sonu only needed to set out three spoons. Mina pouted. "Sonu isn't doing anything."
Mina sat without touching the dishes. Raju had already swept the whole yard.
The dishes stayed piled up. Outside the window, darkness grew.
When Mina finished washing, it was dark. There was no trip to the pools.
Mom stood beside Mina. "You're upset you couldn't go. Tomorrow, wash first, then let's go together."
The next day, Mina washed first, scrubbing even the last dish clean. "Just a little more and I'm done!"
Sunlight still remained. Sitting between Raju and Sonu, Mina pointed to a pool. Tiny fish flipped and splashed.
